blocks.x: Located just two hours from New York City, this historic Hudson Valley village is the perfect escape for leaf peepers and architecture lovers alike.
With its Gilded Age estates, sweeping mountain vistas, and cozy farm-to-table dining scene, Rhinebeck offers the ultimate upstate retreat.
Whether you want to hike to a fire tower or sip craft cocktails in a basement speakeasy, this quaint town has you covered.
Where to stay in this historic village
Rhinebeck seamlessly blends wellness with deep American history.
The Beekman Arms: Book a room at what is widely considered America’s oldest continually operating hotel. It originally opened as a local tavern back in the 1700s.
Mirbeau Inn & Spa: If you want pure relaxation, this 49-room Parisian-style boutique hotel features a luxury spa and an opulent dining room.
Omega Institute: A world-class campus known for weekend yoga, wellness retreats, and all-inclusive stays.

Prussia Frank /Facebook
Exploring nature and vintage planes
The surrounding landscape is breathtaking, offering everything from quiet woodland strolls to high-flying thrills.
Poet’s Walk Park: Located just 10 minutes away in Red Hook, this 120-acre designed landscape features rustic pavilions, sunlit fields, and majestic mountain vistas.
Ferncliff Forest: This 200-acre all-season preserve offers a family-friendly 0.7-mile hike to a fire tower. Climb to the top for incredible panoramic views of the Hudson River.
Old Rhinebeck Aerodrome: See vintage World War 1 aircraft in action. From mid-June through mid-October, you can even strap on a helmet and take a 15-minute tour in a 1929 biplane for $150 per person.

Source / Old Rhinebeck Aerodrome
Gilded Age estates and antique shopping
The Rhinebeck Village Historic District is packed with beautifully preserved architecture and unique local boutiques.
You can browse for artisan goods at Paper Trail, pick up a new read at Oblong Books, or hunt for vintage treasures inside a two-story barn at the Beekman Arms Antique Market.
For a dose of local history, take a short drive to the Wilderstein Historic Site, an 1888 mansion sitting on 40 acres of manicured grounds.
You can also visit the Staatsburgh State Historic Site. This 65-room Beaux Arts masterpiece was built in the late 19th century, and adult admission is just $10.

Source / Wilderstein Historic Site
Where to eat and drink
The local culinary scene is packed with fresh, farm-to-table ingredients and cozy dining rooms.

Coffee & Breakfast: Start your morning with craft coffee at All That Java, or grab a spicy green egg sandwich and fresh pastries from Bread Alone. Golden Russet Cafe & Grocery is another fantastic morning stop housed in a former general store.

Lunch & Dinner: Head to Gigi Hudson Valley for their signature “Skizza” (a local flatbread pie). For upscale dining, book a table at Terrapin, a gorgeous restaurant housed inside a renovated historic church. You can also enjoy expertly prepared French-inspired dishes at Willow, helmed by fine dining chef Charlie Palmer.
Global Flavors: Cinnamon is a local staple serving authentic Indian dishes like Malai Kofta and lamb Ulatiyathu.
Nightlife: Grab a local craft beer on tap at The Kroeg, or hunt down RhineCellar, a secluded cocktail lounge hidden in the basement of the historic hardware building.
Massive fall festivals you cannot miss
If you are planning a trip this October, the Dutchess County Fairgrounds transforms into a massive hub for seasonal events.
Handcrafted Octoberfest (Oct 10-11, 2026): Browse functional pieces from over 100 juried makers. The weekend features a beer garden, live music, a petting zoo, and a giant pumpkin weigh-off.
NYS Sheep & Wool Festival (Oct 17-18, 2026): For nearly 50 years, this massive festival has celebrated the fiber arts with hands-on workshops, livestock exhibits, and hundreds of artisan vendors.

You do not even need a car to visit. You can take the Amtrak train from Penn Station directly to the Rhinecliff station.
If you prefer to drive, the trip takes exactly two hours straight up the Hudson River from New York City.
